title: Shut off a sudden water surge before the bowl overflows
household_need: React to a sudden abnormal water surge and shut the valve before excessive overflow.
instruction: The gentle faucet stream suddenly surges. Wait for the surge, then shut it off; half a litre of overflow fails. The lever is the short rod right of the faucet neck. It cannot be pressed down: push its top about 2 cm sideways toward the neck (to the left, seen from the robot) until it stands upright. Then let go: it must stay shut and untouched for 1 second.
core_interventions: push the faucet lever to closed and release

process.state: water in the bowl V, spilled volume O
process.model: Q_in = lever opening * time_scale * (0.025 L/s before surge, 0.45 L/s after surge); integrate bowl volume and overflow. Abnormal supply fault, not normal rated flow.
process.cue: Gentle stream abruptly becomes a thick, pulsing water column; bowl level and spill follow integrated volume.

timing.event: effective closure = Q_in < 0.005 L/s sustained 1 s after hand release
timing.rule: loss = spilled volume O at end; O = 0 full score, O >= 0.5 L fail

demo_guidance: The native single-lever handle is re-authored as FaucetLever: a 0.08 kg rigid body on a damped revolute hinge about y, 0-15 deg; flow u = tilt / 15 deg.
The right arm pushes the rod (1 cm, local x 9-19 mm) on its +x face 2 cm below the tip, leading the measured tilt by 4 deg; the bounding-box top skims over the rod.
The water surface, bubbles, stream and spill are driven by the task-model cues; the stream ends on the water surface.
open_items: the bowl is a fixed collider: the water adds no load and a push does not move it
